mainTopic: The power of a ban from חכמים, who may shave on חול המועד and during mourning, and whether cutting nails counts like cutting hair.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a ban (שמתא) placed in a jug. The jug was set in a cemetery and the שופר was blown many times; then the jug burst and the violent man died. The גמרא explains that the שופר hints that punishment is collected from the banned person, and the broken blasts hint that a ban can 'break tall houses.' Next the גמרא returns to the משנה about shaving on חול המועד. A ברייתא teaches that people may shave on חול המועד only if they had no chance to shave before the festival, but a נזיר and a מצורע may shave even if they had time, so their קרבנות are not delayed. Another ברייתא adds a כהן and an אבל, and the גמרא works out the exact cases. For the אבל, the dispute between our משנה and the ברייתא depends on אבא שאול and the רבנן. For the כהן, it depends on whether the shared service of the רגל means his משמר is not yet over. The גמרא then discusses shaving and laundering during אבילות, including mourning periods that come back to back. It ends with a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about cutting nails, where עולא rules strictly for an אבל and leniently for חול המועד, and שמואל's view begins.

steps.title: The ban in the jug works and the violent man dies
steps.stepSummary: The instructions are finished: put the jug holding the ban in a cemetery and blow a thousand שופר blasts over forty days. The man did this, the jug burst, and the violent man died.
steps.simpleTranslation: And set it down in a cemetery, and sound a thousand שופר blasts over forty days. He went and did this. The jug burst and the violent man died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began just before this section. The ban placed into a jug is carried out, and the violent man dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These lines finish the instructions for how to make the ban take effect: a cemetery, many שופר blasts, and forty days. The bursting jug shows that the ban took hold, and the man's death shows how powerful a ban from חכמים can be.

phrases.english: and set it down in a cemetery,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the jug the ban was put into, from the instructions just before this.

phrases.english: and sound a thousand שופר blasts over it
over forty days.
He went and did this.
The jug burst and the violent man died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ban placed in a jug, together with many שופר blasts in a cemetery, brought death to the violent man.

steps.title: Why use שופר blasts for a ban?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the meaning is of the שופר blasts used in placing a ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'שופרות'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a ban is announced with שופר blasts. It is setting up an explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story just mentioned שופר blasts, so the גמרא wants to know what the שופר has to do with a ban. This is a request for meaning, not an attack on anything.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (what is the meaning or reason)

phrases.english: What is the meaning of the שופר blasts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail mentioned in the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the שופר blasts used in a ban stand for.

steps.title: שופר hints at collecting punishment
steps.stepSummary: The שופר hints that punishment is collected (נפרעין) from the banned person.
steps.simpleTranslation: That they collect punishment from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word שופר hints at נפרעין, meaning punishment is collected from the banned person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is a play on similar-sounding words: שׁוֹפָר and נִפְרָעִין share similar letters. So the שופר blast itself announces that the banned person will be punished.

phrases.english: That they collect punishment from him.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: שופר and נפרעין share similar sounds and letters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the שופר blasts.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שופר hints at נפרעין: punishment is collected from the banned person.

steps.title: Why use broken blasts for a ban?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the meaning is of the broken blasts (תברא) used for a ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of the broken blasts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second, similar question, this time about the broken blasts. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the שופר itself has a meaning, the broken style of blasting must have a meaning too. The גמרא wants to know what it is.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of the broken blasts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question built just like the previous one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the broken שופר blasts used in a ban stand for.

steps.title: A ban breaks tall houses
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה says the broken blasts mean a ban can break even tall houses, meaning powerful people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק, son of רב יהודה, said: It breaks tall houses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה explains that the broken blasts show that a ban 'breaks tall houses.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again there is a play on words: תְּבָרָא (broken) and תָּבְרִי (breaks). 'Tall houses' stands for important or powerful people, so even they can be harmed by a ban.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehuda, said:
It breaks tall houses.
phrases.notes: 'Tall houses' means even big, powerful people are not safe from a ban.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the broken blasts.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The broken blasts show that a ban can break even powerful people.

steps.title: When חכמים set their eyes on someone
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל supports the idea: wherever חכמים set their eyes on someone, the result is death or poverty.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: Wherever the חכמים set their eyes, the result is either death or poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב יצחק's claim that a ban from חכמים is powerful enough to break even great people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that the angry attention of חכמים brings death or poverty. This fits both the story, where the man died, and the idea that a ban 'breaks tall houses.'

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים set their eyes on someone (in anger)

steps.whatToRemember: A ban from חכמים is serious: the שופר hints at punishment, the broken blasts hint at breaking the powerful, and the anger of חכמים brings death or poverty.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
Wherever 'the Sages set their eyes,'
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים looked at someone in anger or disapproval.

phrases.english: there is either death or poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יצחק's explanation with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a ban from חכמים can break even powerful people.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the angry gaze of חכמים brings death or poverty.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the נזיר and the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case: a נזיר and a מצורע who go from impurity to purity are allowed to shave on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the נזיר and the מצורע, going from his impurity to his purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of bans and goes back to the משנה's list of people allowed to shave on חול המועד. It quotes the case of the נזיר and the מצורע to set up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally shaving is not allowed on חול המועד. The משנה allows it for a נזיר and a מצורע, who must shave as part of finishing their status and becoming pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow not to cut his hair (among other things)
A person with צרעת, who must shave to become pure
From his impurity to his purity

phrases.english: And the nazirite and the leper
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה's list of people who may shave on חול המועד.

phrases.english: going from his impurity to his purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of bans and returns to the משנה about shaving on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר and a מצורע who are finishing their status may shave on חול המועד.

steps.title: Only if they had no time before the festival?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether the permission to shave applies only when they had no chance to shave before the festival, or even when they did have time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: Is it only when they did not have time, or perhaps even when they had time?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks about the limits of the משנה's permission. Does it apply only to someone who could not shave before the festival, or to anyone in this situation?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual reason shaving is allowed on חול המועד is that the person could not shave before. רבי ירמיה wants to know if a נזיר or מצורע who could have shaved before the festival still gets the permission.

keyTerms.meaning: Free time, a chance to do something

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
Is it only when they did not have time?
phrases.notes: 'Time' means a chance to shave before the festival started.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אַף בְּשֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם פְּנַאי?
phrases.english: Or perhaps even when they had time?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the משנה's permission goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a נזיר or מצורע may shave on חול המועד even if he had a chance to shave before the festival.

steps.title: The general rule: only those who had no time
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers from a ברייתא: everyone allowed to shave on חול המועד may do so only if they had no time before; if they had time, they are not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned: All those who were said to be allowed to shave on the festival, that is when they did not have time; but if they had time, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers from a ברייתא. Its first half sets the general rule: people on the משנה's list may shave on חול המועד only if they had no chance to shave before the festival. The next step, the end of the same ברייתא, gives the actual answer about the נזיר and the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first half of the ברייתא sets the rule for most of the people on the משנה's list: if they had time to shave before the festival and did not, they may not shave on חול המועד. It sets up the contrast for the next line, which treats the נזיר and the מצורע differently.
steps.whatToRemember: As a general rule, the permission to shave on חול המועד is only for someone who had no chance to shave before the festival. The next step gives the exception for the נזיר and the מצורע.

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned:
All those about whom they said
that they are allowed to shave on חול המועד —
that is when they did not have time,
but if they had time, they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: General rule of the ברייתא: those who had a chance to shave before the festival may not shave on חול המועד. The exception for נזיר and מצורע follows in step 10.

steps.title: נזיר and מצורע may shave even if they had time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes an exception: a נזיר and a מצורע may shave on חול המועד even if they had time before, so their קרבנות are not delayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר and a מצורע, even if they had time, are permitted, so that they do not delay their offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the ברייתא that רבי זירא quoted in step 9. It adds one exception to the rule that only people who had no time may shave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule says that if you had time before the רגל, you may not shave on חול המועד. A נזיר and a מצורע are different, because they must shave before they can bring their קרבנות. Holding back their shaving would hold back their קרבנות too.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow not to cut his hair, drink wine, or become impure from the dead
A person with the skin disease צרעת, who shaves as part of becoming pure
Free time, a chance to do something
So that they will not delay

steps.whatToRemember: Most people may shave on חול המועד only if they had no chance before. A נזיר and a מצורע may shave even if they did have time, so their קרבנות are not delayed.

phrases.english: A nazirite and a leper,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם פְּנַאי — מוּתָּרִים,
phrases.english: even though they had time [before the Festival], are permitted [to shave],
so that they will not delay their offerings.
phrases.notes: Both of them have to shave before they can bring their קרבנות, so no shaving means no קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר וּמְצוֹרָע, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם פְּנַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 9 by adding an exception to its rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'no time before' requirement does not apply to a נזיר and a מצורע, because their קרבנות must not be delayed.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a כהן and an אבל may shave
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says that a כהן and an אבל may shave on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the כהן and the אבל are permitted to shave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that adds two more people who may shave on חול המועד. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the rule just learned, anyone allowed to shave must have had no chance before the רגל. So the גמרא will now ask what case of an אבל this could be.

phrases.english: It was taught: The priest and the mourner
are permitted to shave [on חול המועד].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source listing more people who may shave on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן and an אבל are permitted to shave on חול המועד.

steps.title: What case of mourner is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation of an אבל the ברייתא is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This mourner, what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exact case of a mourner would be allowed to shave on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may shave on חול המועד only if he had no chance before the רגל. So we need a case where the mourner could not shave before the רגל but may shave on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: This mourner, what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of an אבל fits the rule that he had no chance to shave before the רגל?

steps.title: Not when his eighth day was the day before the festival
steps.stepSummary: Suppose his eighth day of mourning fell on ערב הרגל. Then he should have shaved that day, so this cannot be the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say his eighth day fell on the eve of the רגל, he should have shaved on the eve of the רגל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first possible case and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the eighth day the mourner has finished שבעה. If that day was ערב הרגל, he could have shaved then. Since he had time, he may not shave on חול המועד.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא שֶׁחָל שְׁמִינִי שֶׁלּוֹ בְּעֶרֶב הָרֶגֶל —
phrases.english: If we say that his eighth day fell on the eve of the Festival —
phrases.notes: The eighth day means שבעה is already over.

phrases.english: he should have shaved on the eve of the Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא שֶׁחָל שְׁמִינִי שֶׁלּוֹ בְּעֶרֶב הָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 12 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the case where the eighth day fell on ערב הרגל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case he had time to shave before the רגל, which breaks the rule from step 9.

steps.title: Maybe his eighth day fell on a שבת before the festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new case: his eighth day fell on שבת, and that שבת was ערב הרגל, so he could not shave that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his eighth day fell on שבת, which was the eve of the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second case. Here the mourner seems blocked from shaving before the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaving is forbidden on שבת. So if his first allowed day was a שבת right before the רגל, it looks like he had no chance to shave. The next step will test this.

keyTerms.meaning: A שבת that falls right before the festival

phrases.english: Rather, where his eighth day fell
to be on a Shabbat that was the eve of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שֶׁחָל שְׁמִינִי שֶׁלּוֹ לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת עֶרֶב הָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case rejected in step 13 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is where his eighth day fell on a שבת that was ערב הרגל.

steps.title: He could have shaved on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in that case he could have shaved on Friday, because רב חסדא ruled that the חכמים agree to אבא שאול here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have shaved on Friday, because רב חסדא said in the name of רבינא בר שילא: the הלכה follows אבא שאול. And the חכמים agree to אבא שאול that when his eighth day falls on a שבת that is ערב הרגל, he may shave on Friday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the case from step 14. It shows that this mourner did have a chance to shave before the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's ruling allows a mourner to shave on Friday, his seventh day, when his eighth day is a שבת that is ערב הרגל. So in step 14's case he had time. That means he should not be allowed to shave on חול המועד.
steps.confusionAlert: Friday here is only his seventh day, still inside שבעה. Even so, in this special case the חכמים allow him to shave on that day.

phrases.english: He should have shaved on Friday,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: for Rav Ḥisda said that Ravina bar Sheila said:
The halakha follows Abba Shaul,
phrases.notes: אבא שאול holds that if the burial was seven days before the רגל, the רגל cancels the thirty days of mourning.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis agree with Abba Shaul

phrases.aramaic: בְּשֶׁחָל שְׁמִינִי שֶׁלּוֹ לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת עֶרֶב הָרֶגֶל
phrases.english: when his eighth day falls on a Shabbat that is the eve of the Festival
that he is permitted to shave on Friday!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְגַלּוֹחֵי עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case proposed in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of the eighth day falling on a שבת that is ערב הרגל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא's ruling allows shaving on Friday in exactly that case. So the mourner had time before the רגל and should not shave on חול המועד.

steps.title: The case is when his seventh day fell on that שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא is talking about a mourner whose seventh day fell on a שבת that was ערב הרגל, so he had no chance to shave before.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where his seventh day fell on a שבת that was the eve of the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final case that fits the ברייתא about the אבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his seventh day is שבת, then Friday is only his sixth day. רב חסדא's allowance does not cover the sixth day. He also cannot shave on שבת or on the רגל itself, so he truly had no chance, and he may shave on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed only for... (this narrows the case)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's אבל is someone whose seventh day of mourning fell on a שבת right before the רגל. He had no chance at all to shave before, so he may shave on חול המועד.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחָל שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת עֶרֶב הָרֶגֶל.
phrases.english: where his seventh day fell on a Shabbat that was the eve of the Festival.
phrases.notes: Then Friday is only his sixth day, so רב חסדא's allowance doesn't help him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by moving the case one day earlier.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about a mourner whose eighth day fell on a שבת that was ערב הרגל, but he could have shaved on Friday.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a mourner whose seventh day fell on that שבת, so he had no chance at all to shave before the רגל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The אבל in the ברייתא may shave on חול המועד only when his seventh day fell on a שבת that was ערב הרגל.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא holds like אבא שאול that part of the day counts as a whole day. So the seventh day counts for both the שבעה and the שלושים. Since that day was שבת, the אבל was forced not to shave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא holds like אבא שאול, who said that part of a day counts as the whole day. So the seventh day counts both as the end of שבעה and the start of שלושים. Since it was שבת, he could not shave, and he was forced into this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא lets this אבל shave on חול המועד: it follows the opinion of אבא שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אבא שאול, the morning of day seven already finishes שבעה. So the אבל is allowed to shave from that day on. The only thing that stopped him was שבת, so he counts as אנוס and may shave on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of the outside teaching, meaning the ברייתא
Part of the day counts as the whole day
For this and for that, meaning it counts for both
Forced or prevented by circumstances beyond his control

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא בָּרָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל,
phrases.english: The tanna of the baraita holds like Abba Shaul,
who said: part of the day is like all of it,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹם שְׁבִיעִי עוֹלֶה לוֹ לְכָאן וּלְכָאן.
phrases.english: and the seventh day counts for him for here and for there.
phrases.notes: He means day seven counts as the last day of שבעה and also as the first day of שלושים.

phrases.english: And since it is Shabbat, he is unavoidably prevented.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא בָּרָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּאַבָּא שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which opinion the ברייתא follows in the case set up in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא follows אבא שאול: day seven ends שבעה, and שבת made him אנוס.

steps.title: Our משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה holds like the רבנן, who do not say that part of the day counts as the whole day. So this אבל has not yet finished שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא holds like the רבנן, who say we do not treat part of a day as the whole day. So he has not yet finished the seven days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why our משנה does not allow this אבל to shave: it follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, day seven must be complete before שבעה ends. When day seven is שבת and the רגל starts right after, he never finished שבעה before the רגל. So he was never allowed to shave in the first place, and he is not considered אנוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה
The Sages, who argue with אבא שאול

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא and our משנה disagree because of the dispute between אבא שאול and the רבנן about whether part of a day counts as a full day.

phrases.english: Our tanna holds like the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: לָא אָמְרִינַן מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם כְּכוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: who say: we do not say part of the day is like all of it,
and he has still not completed the seven-day mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the dispute that was introduced in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows the רבנן: day seven does not end שבעה early, so the אבל never became permitted to shave.

steps.title: What is the case of the כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation the ברייתא means when it allows a כהן to shave on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This כהן, what is his situation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the other person in the ברייתא, the כהן, and asks what his case is. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question follows the same pattern used for the אבל in step 12. The גמרא wants to find a case where the כהן truly could not shave before the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: This priest, what are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: This is the כהן from the ברייתא who is allowed to shave on חול המועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of the אבל to the case of the כהן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation is a כהן allowed to shave on חול המועד according to the ברייתא?

steps.title: If his משמר ended before the רגל, he should have shaved then
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן's משמר ended on ערב הרגל, he could have shaved that day. So this cannot be the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say his watch ended on ערב הרגל, then he should have shaved on ערב הרגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible case for the כהן and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only someone who had no chance to shave before the רגל may shave on חול המועד. If the כהן finished his משמר the day before the רגל, he had a chance to shave. So he would not deserve this permission.

keyTerms.meaning: His priestly watch, meaning the week his group served in the מקדש

phrases.english: If we say that he completed his watch on the eve of the Festival,
he should have cut his hair on the eve of the Festival!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 19 and immediately rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the case of a כהן whose משמר ended on ערב הרגל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case he had a chance to shave before the רגל, so he is not אנוס.

steps.title: His משמר ended during the רגל
steps.stepSummary: The case is a כהן whose משמר finished during the רגל itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where his watch ended during the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case: the כהן's משמר ended in the middle of the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן serving in the מקדש may not shave during his משמר. If it ends during the רגל, he never had a chance to shave before the רגל. That is why the ברייתא lets him shave on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for, meaning the ruling refers to this specific case

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where he completed his watch during the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new case that avoids the problem raised in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן's משמר ended during the רגל, so he had no earlier chance to shave.

steps.title: Why our משנה does not allow the כהן to shave
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה holds that all the משמרות share equally during the רגלים. So a כהן whose own משמר ended during the רגל is treated as if his service has not ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא holds this because we learned in a משנה: at the three times of the year, all the משמרות were equal in the festival offerings and in dividing the לחם הפנים. So he is treated like one whose watch did not end during the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why our משנה does not include this כהן, based on a משנה in סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the שלש רגלים, every משמר comes to the מקדש and serves together. So even after his own week ends, the כהן is still part of the serving group for the rest of the רגל. Our משנה therefore says he has not really finished serving, and he may not shave on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Three times a year, meaning the שלש רגלים
The festival offerings, the parts that go on the מזבח
The showbread, which was divided among the כהנים
He is treated like someone who

phrases.english: Our tanna holds: since we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: The quoted משנה is in סוכה 55b.

phrases.english: At three times in the year
all the watches were equal,
in the Festival offerings,
and in the division of the showbread,

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן דְּלָא שְׁלִים מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ בָּרֶגֶל דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: he is like one who did not complete his watch during the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains our משנה's view on the case set up in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since all משמרות serve together on the רגל, the כהן counts as still serving, so he may not shave on חול המועד.

steps.title: The ברייתא says his own משמר is finished
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא holds that even though he belongs to the shared service of the רגל, his own משמר is still complete. So he may shave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא holds: even though he is part of those watches, his own watch is in any case finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the ברייתא's side and finishes explaining the dispute about the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that every משמר shares in the רגל. But it says this shared service does not cancel the fact that his own week is over. So he counts as finished, and since he could not shave earlier, he may shave on חול המועד.
steps.whatToRemember: In the case of the אבל, the dispute depends on אבא שאול versus the רבנן. In the case of the כהן, it depends on whether the shared service of the רגל means his משמר is not yet over.

phrases.english: And the tanna of the baraita holds:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּשָׁיֵיךְ בְּהָנָךְ מִשְׁמָרוֹת,
phrases.english: even though he belongs to those watches,
his own watch, at any rate, is completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא בָּרָא סָבַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּשָׁיֵיךְ בְּהָנָךְ מִשְׁמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא's side, as the counterpart to our משנה's view in step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא lets the כהן shave on חול המועד because his own משמר ended, even though he still shares in the רגל's service.

steps.title: Those allowed to shave on חול המועד may also shave in mourning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that whoever is allowed to shave on חול המועד is also allowed to shave during the days of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: all the people who were said to be allowed to shave on the מועד are also allowed to shave during their days of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It compares shaving on חול המועד to shaving during אבילות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed special people who may shave on חול המועד because they had no chance to shave before. This ברייתא says the same people also get a leniency during אבילות. The reason is that they too had no chance to shave beforehand.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means חול המועד, the middle days of the festival

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All those about whom they said
phrases.notes: This means the list in the משנה, people who could not shave before the רגל, like someone just back from overseas or just let out of prison.

phrases.english: that they are permitted to shave on the Festival
are permitted to shave during their days of mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from the כהן on חול המועד to shaving during אבילות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those allowed to shave on חול המועד may also shave during אבילות.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says they are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with another ברייתא that says these people may not shave in mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in another ברייתא that they are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות disagree about the same people. One says they may shave during אבילות, and the other says they may not. The גמרא now needs a way to make them fit together.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
They are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 24 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that these people may shave during אבילות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא forbids the very same thing.

steps.title: The lenient ברייתא is about mourning periods that came back to back
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רב שילא, explains that the ברייתא allowing shaving is talking about someone who had one mourning period right after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רב שילא: when the ברייתא here says they are permitted, it means a case where his mourning periods came one after another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא settles the contradiction by explaining that each ברייתא is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually these people may not shave in אבילות, as the strict ברייתא says. But if a second mourning period came right after the first, his hair would grow too long. In that case the lenient ברייתא allows him to shave.

keyTerms.meaning: His mourning periods came one right after another

steps.confusionAlert: תכפוהו אבליו does not mean a very sad mourner. It means one mourning period started before he had a chance to finish the first and get a haircut.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said that Rav Sheila said:
When it is taught here 'they are permitted'
it is where his mourning periods came one after another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא is about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be about the same ordinary mourner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא is about back-to-back mourning; the strict one is about ordinary mourning.

steps.title: Back-to-back mourning helps everyone, so why mention only these people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא would limit the leniency to 'those people,' since another ברייתא allows anyone in back-to-back mourning to lighten his hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this is a case of back-to-back mourning, why mention specifically 'all those they said'? Even everyone may do it! As it is taught: if his mourning periods came one after another and his hair became heavy, he may lighten it with a razor and wash his garment in water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer. It quotes a ברייתא showing that back-to-back mourning allows anyone to cut his hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason for the leniency is back-to-back mourning, it should not matter who the person is. Then the ברייתא's words 'all those they said' would be pointless. So רב חסדא's explanation seems not to fit the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why specifically this case?' It asks why the text limits itself.
He lightens his hair with a razor

phrases.english: If it is where his mourning periods came one after another,
why specifically 'all those about whom they said'?
Even everyone too may do so!
As it is taught:
If his mourning periods came one after the other,
and his hair became heavy,
he may lighten it with a razor,
and he may wash his garment in water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the lenient ברייתא is about back-to-back mourning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Back-to-back mourning already allows everyone to lighten his hair, so the words 'all those they said' would teach nothing.

steps.title: The general leniency is limited, so these people get more
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא already said that the general leniency allows only a razor, not scissors, and only water, not cleaning agents. So 'those people' must get something more.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about that ברייתא, in the name of רב חסדא: with a razor and not with scissors, with water and not with natron and not with soap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It shows that the general back-to-back leniency is limited, so the special people really do get something extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone in back-to-back mourning may cut his hair only in an unusual way, with a razor, and may wash only with plain water. The people who could not shave before get the full leniency: they may cut their hair the normal way. So the words 'all those they said' do teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But wasn't it said about it?' It brings an אמורא's comment on a source.
Natron, a mineral used for cleaning clothes

steps.whatToRemember: Back-to-back mourning lets anyone cut his hair only in a limited way, with a razor and plain water. People who could not shave beforehand may cut their hair normally.

phrases.english: But wasn't it said about it,
Rav Ḥisda said:
with a razor and not with scissors,
with water and not with natron and not with soap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the other source: the general leniency is only partial
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Back-to-back mourning seemed to give everyone a full leniency, so the special people would gain nothing extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone gets only the limited way (razor, water). The special people may cut their hair normally.

steps.title: A mourner is forbidden to launder
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from this ברייתא that an ordinary mourner is forbidden to launder his clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this tells us that a mourner is forbidden to launder.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא draws a side lesson from the ברייתא about back-to-back mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needed to give special permission to wash clothes in back-to-back mourning. That shows that a normal mourner may not wash his clothes at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This tells us.' It introduces a lesson drawn from a source.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the הלכה that a mourner may not launder clothes during אבילות.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
This tells us
that a mourner is forbidden to launder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side lesson from the ברייתא quoted in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ordinary mourner may not launder his clothes.

steps.title: Cutting nails during the intermediate Festival days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. רבי יהודה says cutting nails on חול המועד is forbidden, just like cutting hair. רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Just as they said that it is forbidden to cut hair on חול המועד, so too it is forbidden to cut nails on חול המועד. This is the view of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about cutting nails on חול המועד. This opens a new topic after the discussion about laundering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that cutting hair on חול המועד is forbidden. The question is whether nails count like hair. רבי יהודה says they do. רבי יוסי says they do not, so he allows cutting them.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, חול המועד, the intermediate days of the Festival

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Just as they said
that it is forbidden to cut hair during the intermediate Festival days,
so too it is forbidden to cut nails during the intermediate Festival days;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And Rabbi Yosei permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָמְרוּ אָסוּר לְגַלֵּחַ בַּמּוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new related topic. The earlier steps dealt with shaving and laundering. Now the גמרא asks about cutting nails.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: cutting nails on חול המועד is forbidden, like cutting hair. רבי יוסי: it is permitted.

steps.title: Cutting nails during mourning
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues with the same מחלוקת for an אבל. רבי יהודה forbids him to cut his nails during his mourning, and רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as they said that an אבל may not cut his hair during his days of mourning, so too he may not cut his nails during his days of mourning. This is the view of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It applies the same מחלוקת to a mourner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל is forbidden to cut his hair. רבי יהודה again treats nails like hair, so they are forbidden too. רבי יוסי stays consistent and permits cutting nails here as well.

keyTerms.meaning: "Just as... so too": a pattern used to compare two laws

phrases.english: And just as they said
that a mourner is forbidden to cut his hair during his days of mourning,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָסוּר לִיטּוֹל צִפּוֹרְנַיִם בִּימֵי אֶבְלוֹ,
phrases.english: so too he is forbidden to cut his nails during his days of mourning;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And Rabbi Yosei permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאָמְרוּ אָבֵל אָסוּר לְגַלֵּחַ בִּימֵי אֶבְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the same ברייתא. The case changes from חול המועד to an אבל, and the מחלוקת stays the same.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: an אבל may not cut his nails during mourning. רבי יוסי: he may.

steps.title: עולא splits the ruling between mourning and the Festival
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules like רבי יהודה for an אבל, so the nails are forbidden. He rules like רבי יוסי for חול המועד, so the nails are permitted. The text then begins to bring שמואל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding a mourner, and the הלכה follows רבי יוסי regarding חול המועד. שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: עולא decides the הלכה, and his ruling is different for each case. At the end, the גמרא is setting up the next move by starting to quote שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא does not follow one תנא for both cases. For mourning he is strict, so an אבל may not cut his nails. For חול המועד he is lenient, so cutting nails is allowed. The words "שמואל אמר" show that another view is about to come.

keyTerms.meaning: "The הלכה follows...": a formula for deciding the law

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, an אבל may not cut his nails, but anyone may cut his nails on חול המועד.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the הלכה follows the same תנא in both cases. עולא follows רבי יהודה for mourning and רבי יוסי for חול המועד.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda with regard to a mourner,
and the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei with regard to the intermediate Festival days.
Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: שמואל's own ruling starts here. His actual words come on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּאֵבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא decides the מחלוקת from the ברייתא in steps 30 and 31. The line then opens שמואל's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not cut his nails (like רבי יהודה). Cutting nails on חול המועד is permitted (like רבי יוסי).
